problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={t}^{2}-1,\,y={e}^{-4t}.$ Given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{-2{e}^{-4t}}{t},$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$

feedback.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={t}^{2}+2,\,y={t}^{4}+{t}^{2}.$ Given  that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2{t}^{2}+1,$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2{t}^{2}+1,$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}({t}^{2}+2)=2t
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2{t}^{2}+1)}{2t} \\  & =\frac{4t}{2t} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
